subject: Cluster sizing & activation velocity options for NovaGene

Subject: Cluster sizing & activation velocity options for NovaGene

Hi Amanda —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Based on the workload samples you shared (mix of batched inference for 20–30 concurrent streams and latency-sensitive user-facing chat), I put together three deployment options that balance latency, unit cost, and ramp speed. I attached a quick worksheet with the numbers. High-level:

Option A — Fast-start small cluster (low upfront commit)
- Initial cluster: 8x A100 equivalent GPUs (single availability zone)
- Minimum guaranteed: 4 GPUs (warm lanes)
- Ramp: add 4 GPUs after 30 days if sustained 70% utilization
- Use-case: short pilot + quick production cutover, higher unit cost but rapid activation

Option B — Phased performance lane (recommended for prod)
- Initial cluster: 24x A100 equivalent GPUs across 2 AZs
- Minimum guaranteed: 12 GPUs (distributed warm capacity)
- Ramp schedule: +8 GPUs at month 2, +4 GPUs at month 4 tied to usage thresholds
- Includes KV prefix caching and prioritized prewarming for chat workloads

Option C — Anchored throughput (lower unit cost, longer lead)
- Initial cluster: 64x A100 equivalent GPUs (multi-AZ, reserved pool)
- Minimum guaranteed: 32 GPUs
- Ramp: linear scaling over 180 days with quarterly checkpoints
- Use-case: enterprise steady-state with cost efficiency and headroom for burst

Tradeoffs and notes:
- We can shorten Option B's month-2 trigger to 30 days for a small activation fee; this helps customers peak into production sooner.
- Latency SLOs and auto-fallbacks to smaller model variants are included in all options.
- Pricing in the worksheet shows committed-rate discounts and warm-start credits.

Next steps: pick a preferred option and I’ll loop in Technical Ops (Camila) to validate the cluster topology and finalize warmup windows. If Procurement wants an alternative minimum (e.g., 8 GPUs instead of 12 for Option B) we can model the cost impact.

Best,
Ben

Ben — quick answers below, feel free to paste into the reply. Happy to join the technical call (tomorrow 10am PT works).

1) Minimum billing model: For Option B the 12-GPU minimum is a guaranteed reserved footprint — billed continuously at the committed rate. We apply warm-start credits on top for prefix/KV cache memory which lowers effective per-token cost during the early weeks. We can offer a partial-prorate for customers requesting a true variable billing model, but that moves them closer to a consumption offer (higher unit price, lower commit).

2) Warm-start credits (Option A): 200k token-equivalent prefix cache credit per warm lane for 30 days, plus 48 hours of prioritized prewarm for the model family. We include a one-time warmup runbook to reduce cold-start tail latency.

3) Multi-AZ lead time (Option C): To guarantee full multi-AZ placement at 64 GPUs we need a 6–8 week provisioning window to align capacity and networking, shorter if the customer accepts single-AZ fallback for the first 2 weeks.

Notes: If Procurement requests a 10-GPU minimum instead of 12 on Option B, the cost delta is ~9% annualized; I can include that scenario in the worksheet.

Camila
Technical Operations
Redwood Inference

Amanda — thanks for the quick read. Answers inline from our ops team and next steps below.

1) Billing on minimums: Option B is a continuous reserved minimum (12 GPUs billed at committed rate). We can model a hybrid (10-GPU minimum + consumption overflow) — that increases unit price by ~9% but reduces committed spend.

2) Warm-start credits: For Option A we include 200k token-equivalent cache credit per warm lane for 30 days and a 48-hour prioritized prewarm window. We'll schedule a prewarm run to validate latency targets.

3) Lead time for multi-AZ: 6–8 weeks to guarantee multi-AZ placement for the full 64-GPU pool; can do single-AZ immediately with multi-AZ follow-up.

DocuSign & timing: I updated the worksheet to include the 10-GPU hybrid scenario and a version of Option B with a 30-day early trigger (activation fee of $7,500). If Procurement is comfortable with Option B (12-GPU minimum), I can send a Ballpark DocuSign by Friday and schedule the technical call for tomorrow 10am PT with Camila.

Proposed next steps:
- Amanda / Procurement: confirm preferred option or request the 10-GPU hybrid model
- Technical call: Tue 10 Dec, 10:00am PT (Camila to lead)
- DocuSign: Ben to send ballpark by EOD Fri if Option B chosen

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Ben
